message.content:
Below are two ways to spin up a **Google Cloud Compute Engine** instance that has an **NVIDIA RTX A6000** GPU and boots from **Ubuntu 20.04 LTS**.

> ⚠️ **Important**  
> * Google Cloud does **not** use the “EC2” terminology – that’s AWS.  
> * You must have a Google Cloud project with billing enabled, the **Compute Engine API** turned on, and a **service account** (or user credentials) that has the `roles/compute.instanceAdmin.v1` role.  
> * The GPU type you’re looking for is `nvidia-tesla-a6000`.  
> * The GPU must be attached to a **GPU‑enabled zone** (e.g., `us-central1-b`, `us-east1-c`, `europe-west4-a`, etc.).  
> * The instance must be created with a machine type that supports GPUs (e.g., `n1-standard-8`, `n1-highmem-8`, `n1-highcpu-8`, etc.).  

---

## 1. Using the `gcloud` CLI

```bash
# Variables
PROJECT="my-gcp-project"
ZONE="us-central1-b"          # pick a GPU‑enabled zone
INSTANCE_NAME="rtx-a6000-ubuntu"
MACHINE_TYPE="n1-standard-8"  # 8 vCPUs, 30 GB RAM
GPU_COUNT=1
GPU_TYPE="nvidia-tesla-a6000"
IMAGE_FAMILY="ubuntu-2004-lts"
IMAGE_PROJECT="ubuntu-os-cloud"

# Create the instance
gcloud compute instances create "$INSTANCE_NAME" \
  --project="$PROJECT" \
  --zone="$ZONE" \
  --machine-type="$MACHINE_TYPE" \
  --accelerator=type="$GPU_TYPE,count=$GPU_COUNT" \
  --image-family="$IMAGE_FAMILY" \
  --image-project="$IMAGE_PROJECT" \
  --boot-disk-size=100GB \
  --boot-disk-type=pd-ssd \
  --scopes=https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud-platform \
  --metadata-from-file startup-script=startup.sh   # optional: your init script
```

### What the command does

| Flag | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| `--machine-type` | CPU/RAM configuration |
| `--accelerator` | Attach the GPU(s) |
| `--image-family` & `--image-project` | Pick Ubuntu 20.04 LTS |
| `--boot-disk-size` | Size of the root disk |
| `--scopes` | Grant the instance full Cloud Platform access (needed for GPU drivers) |
| `--metadata-from-file startup-script` | Optional: run a shell script after boot (e.g., install NVIDIA drivers) |

> **Tip:** If you want the instance to automatically install the NVIDIA driver, add a `startup.sh` script that runs `sudo apt-get update && sudo apt-get install -y nvidia-driver-535` (or the latest driver for A6000).

---

## 2. Using the REST API (curl)

If you prefer to call the API directly (e.g., from a CI/CD pipeline), you can POST a JSON payload to the Compute Engine endpoint.

```bash
# Variables
PROJECT="my-gcp-project"
ZONE="us-central1-b"
INSTANCE_NAME="rtx-a6000-ubuntu"
MACHINE_TYPE="n1-standard-8"
GPU_COUNT=1
GPU_TYPE="nvidia-tesla-a6000"
IMAGE_FAMILY="ubuntu-2004-lts"
IMAGE_PROJECT="ubuntu-os-cloud"

# Build the JSON body
cat <<EOF > instance.json
{
  "name": "$INSTANCE_NAME",
  "machineType": "zones/$ZONE/machineTypes/$MACHINE_TYPE",
  "disks": [
    {
      "boot": true,
      "autoDelete": true,
      "initializeParams": {
        "sourceImage": "projects/$IMAGE_PROJECT/global/images/family/$IMAGE_FAMILY",
        "diskSizeGb": 100,
        "diskType": "projects/$PROJECT/zones/$ZONE/diskTypes/pd-ssd"
      }
    }
  ],
  "networkInterfaces": [
    {
      "network": "global/networks/default",
      "accessConfigs": [
        { "type": "ONE_TO_ONE_NAT", "name": "External NAT" }
      ]
    }
  ],
  "guestAccelerators": [
    {
      "acceleratorType": "projects/$PROJECT/zones/$ZONE/acceleratorTypes/$GPU_TYPE",
      "acceleratorCount": $GPU_COUNT
    }
  ],
  "serviceAccounts": [
    {
      "email": "default",
      "scopes": [
        "https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud-platform"
      ]
    }
  ],
  "metadata": {
    "items": [
      {
        "key": "startup-script",
        "value": "#!/bin/bash\napt-get update\napt-get install -y nvidia-driver-535\n"
      }
    ]
  }
}
EOF

# Call the API (replace <ACCESS_TOKEN> with a valid OAuth 2.0 token)
curl -X POST \
  "https://compute.googleapis.com/compute/v1/projects/$PROJECT/zones/$ZONE/instances" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <ACCESS_TOKEN>" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d @instance.json
```

### Notes on the JSON payload

- **`machineType`** – fully‑qualified path to the machine type.  
- **`guestAccelerators`** – attaches the GPU.  
- **`disks.initializeParams.sourceImage`** – pulls the Ubuntu 20.04 LTS image from the `ubuntu-os-cloud` project.  
- **`metadata.startup-script`** – optional but handy for installing NVIDIA drivers automatically.  
- **`serviceAccounts.scopes`** – gives the instance permission to install drivers and access other Cloud services.

---

## Quick Checklist

| ✅ | Item |
|----|------|
| 1 | Project has billing enabled. |
| 2 | Compute Engine API is enabled. |
| 3 | GPU‑enabled zone selected. |
| 4 | Machine type supports GPUs. |
| 5 | Service account has `compute.instanceAdmin.v1` role. |
| 6 | (Optional) Startup script installs NVIDIA driver. |

Once the instance is running, you can SSH into it and verify the GPU:

```bash
ssh ubuntu@$INSTANCE_IP
nvidia-smi
```

You should see the RTX A6000 listed with its driver version. Happy computing!
